selected_evidence.requirement: Nightly dated backup from node2 to node1
selected_evidence.summary: Shows the 02:15 daily cron schedule, active cron service, successful end-to-end backup, and valid dated archive `/var/backups/inventory/inventory-2026-10-02.tar.gz`.
The protected source probe and archived copy had identical SHA-256 hashes.
The retention test removed an eight-day-old candidate and preserved a six-day-old candidate.
A dedicated key was generated on node1 and restricted on node2 to the inventory export command.
Healthy baseline boot ID `1a816f1f-…`, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID `9a95a1a9-…`, and successful post-restart backup recovery.
Healthy baseline boot ID `0571f4dd-…`, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID `fdbee2b4-…`, restored SSH/export state, and successful end-to-end backup after recovery.

#!/bin/sh
set -eu
umask 077
DEST=/var/backups/inventory
STAMP=$(/bin/date +%F)
FINAL="$DEST/inventory-$STAMP.tar.gz"
TEMP="$DEST/.inventory-$STAMP.$$.tmp"
trap '/bin/rm -f "$TEMP"' EXIT HUP INT TERM
/usr/bin/flock -n /run/lock/inventory-backup.lock /usr/bin/ssh -i /root/.ssh/inventory_backup_ed25519 -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes -o UserKnownHostsFile=/root/.ssh/known_hosts_inventory root@10.100.216.11 backup > "$TEMP"
/bin/test -s "$TEMP"
/bin/tar -tzf "$TEMP" >/dev/null
/bin/mv -f "$TEMP" "$FINAL"
/usr/bin/find "$DEST" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name 'inventory-*.tar.gz' -mtime +6 -delete
trap - EXIT HUP INT TERM
EOF
sudo chmod 750 /usr/local/sbin/inventory-backup
sudo tee /etc/cron.d/inventory-backup >/dev/null <<'EOF'
SHELL=/bin/sh
PATH=/sbin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin
15 2 * * * root /usr/local/sbin/inventory-backup >>/var/log/inventory-backup.log 2>&1
EOF
sudo chmod 644 /etc/cron.d/inventory-backup
if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo restorecon -F /usr/local/sbin/inventory-backup /etc/cron.d/inventory-backup /var/backups/inventory /root/.ssh/known_hosts_inventory; fi

sudo cat /etc/cron.d/inventory-backup
sudo find /var/backups/inventory -maxdepth 1 -type f -printf '%f %s bytes %TY-%Tm-%Td %TH:%TM:%TS\n' | sort
